title: Nueva York amplía la regulación para desarrolladores de Inteligencia Artificial
content:
Nueva York exigirá por ley que, a partir de noviembre, los desarrolladores de inteligencia artificial (IA) de vanguardia se registren ante el Estado y cumplan con estrictos estándares "de transparencia, seguridad e informes de incidentes", anunció este lunes la gobernadora Kathy Hochul.
La nueva regulación, en cumplimiento con la Ley de Seguridad y Educación en IA Responsable (Ley RAISE, por sus siglas en inglés), aprobada el año pasado por la legislatura estatal, exigirá que, a partir de enero, informen sobre incidentes críticos de seguridad en un plazo de 72 horas y proporcionen informes periódicos a la nueva Oficina de Innovación Digital, Gobernanza, Integridad y Confianza (DIGIT) del Estado.
Las empresas que no cumplan con las normas se enfrentarán a sanciones civiles.
Hochul anunció además el nombramiento del abogado Marc Gilman como director adjunto de la nueva Oficina de Innovación Digital, creada el pasado diciembre, de quien dijo que aporta años de experiencia en gestión de riesgos tecnológicos y cumplimiento normativo.
"A medida que esta tecnología evoluciona, utilizaremos todas las herramientas disponibles a nivel estatal para proteger a los neoyorquinos. Analizaremos detenidamente otras maneras de ampliar la Ley RAISE y fortalecer nuestras leyes sobre IA", indicó Hochul.

Incluso, dijo que no descarta explorar medidas de seguridad "como los interruptores de apagado automático de la IA si se consideran viables y beneficiosas para nuestro estado", algo que también evalúa California.
"En contraste con lo que acabo de decir sobre la importancia de actuar con urgencia, mañana Donald Trump se dirigirá a los líderes mundiales en la Asamblea General de la ONU. Recurrirá a sus tácticas habituales. Insultará a nuestros aliados. Incluso podría amenazar con anexar otra nación soberana. Pero lo que no escucharán es un plan serio y bien pensado para regular la inteligencia artificial", afirmó la demócrata.
Trump ha rechazado poner freno al desarrollo de la IA, como han sugerido los líderes del sector tecnológico, y, al contrario, ha dicho que creará la Fuerza IA y designará a un zar. De acuerdo con el mandatario, con las leyes existentes puede vigilarse esta tecnología sin necesidad de ralentizar su desarrollo y mantener la supremacía de EE.UU. en IA sobre China.
"Negarse a cumplir con sus responsabilidades, negarse a tomar en serio la regulación de la IA -quizás debido a sus inversiones personales en empresas de IA- constituye una abdicación de responsabilidad de proporciones épicas", aseguró Hochul.

La gobernadora hizo un llamado a la Administración Trump y a los líderes mundiales "para que den un paso al frente y se unan a nosotros, porque no puede ser solo Nueva York. No puede ser solo California. No pueden ser solo un puñado de gobernadores. Necesitamos una estrategia nacional y global".
El pasado viernes, el gobernador de California, Gavin Newsom, firmó una orden ejecutiva que endurece la vigilancia sobre las empresas de IA de ese estado y ordenó a su equipo evaluar la creación de un 'interruptor de apagado' obligatorio para los modelos de IA más avanzados, así como la instalación permanente de auditores independientes dentro de los laboratorios de las principales empresas del sector.

title: Fishermen risk lives to save newborn Elephant in northeastern India (Video)
content:
In a dramatic rescue, a 3-4-day-old elephant calf swept away by the strong currents of the Teesta River in northeastern India was rescued by local fishermen and reunited with its mother after nearly two hours of efforts.
The calf was separated from its mother while crossing the river and was swept downstream from the upper section of the Teesta Barrage. After spotting the helpless calf struggling in the current, fishermen Ajay Das, Rajesh Das, Gopal Das, Mittu Das and Bishwanath Das risked their lives to pull it from the water and bring it safely to a river island.
Forest personnel from the Baikunthapur Forest Division soon joined the rescue operation and began efforts to locate the mother.
The calf continued calling for its mother, prompting an emotional search. After nearly two hours, the rescue team successfully reunited the newborn with its mother in the Teesta’s river-island area at Gajoldoba.
The rescue has been hailed locally as a heartwarming example of compassion and wildlife conservation. (Darjeeling Chronicle)

title: Aux Comores, une activité de ramassage des déchets pointe la défaillance du système de collecte
content:
Aux Comores, une activité de ramassage des déchets pointe la défaillance du système de collecte
Aux Comores, les opérations de nettoyage du littoral se multiplient, mais les déchets reviennent souvent quelques jours plus tard. À Iconi, associations, ministère de l’Environnement, pêcheurs et habitants se sont mobilisés à l’occasion de la Journée mondiale du nettoyage, dimanche 20 septembre.
Publié le : Modifié le :
De notre envoyé spécial à Iconi, Abdallah Mzembaba
Sur la plage Ikoju Ibambouba d'Iconi, non loin de Moroni, la capitale des Comores, les différents acteurs s’affairent pour nettoyer le littoral jonché de bouteilles en plastique, de tissus, de ferraille... Mais une fois les déchets ramassés, une difficulté très concrète se pose : les défenseurs de l’environnement ne disposent pas d’endroit identifié pour déposer les déchets.
« Pour l’instant, nous sommes dans des discussions avec des responsables de l’État et de notre localité pour prendre des mesures et pour qu’ils nous donnent des endroits, parce que c’est là où il y a le problème », explique Mhoma Mnahoula Saindou secrétaire général de l’Union des jeunes de Mtsamboutsini.
À lire aussiComores: à Moroni, une opération citoyenne pour assainir la Baie de Kalaweni
Dans plusieurs communes, des dispositifs de collecte existent déjà. Ce qui n’est pas le cas partout. Entre ramassage, stockage et traitement, plusieurs maillons restent défaillants et compliquent encore la lutte contre la pollution du littoral. « Les déchets reviennent parce que la problématique des déchets c'est une chaîne de valeur », développe Salima Hamada, coordinatrice du projet Adaptation basée sur les écosystèmes. « Il faut avoir un bon système de collecte des déchets. Il faut les entreposer dans des décharges. Nous n'avons pas encore un système proprement dit de gestion des déchets. Il y a des initiatives qui sont prises par les communes, mais la collecte n'est pas suffisante », regrette-t-elle.
À Iconi, la coopérative des pêcheurs récupère les déchets plastiques qui seront recyclés par une entreprise, mais rien n'est prévu pour les autres types de déchets. Si aujourd’hui les déchets ont été jetés dans la décharge d’Itsundzu, située à plusieurs kilomètres d’Iconi, cette action met surtout en lumière les limites de la gestion des déchets dans l’archipel.

title: Menina com deficiência vibra ao andar de skate adaptado em SP; vídeo
content:
Menina com deficiência vibra ao andar de skate adaptado em SP; vídeo
Os gritos de alegria de Lívia dizem tudo. A menina com deficiência usou um skate adaptado para participar de uma atividade do projeto Skate Anima, em São Paulo, e passou a descida inteira sorrindo, gritando e vibrando com a experiência.
O Só Notícia Boa já mostrou o trabalho do Skate Anima em 2019, quando João Vicente, então com 7 anos, conseguiu realizar o sonho de andar de skate com a ajuda de uma estrutura adaptada. Sete anos depois, o projeto continua promovendo vivências para pessoas com deficiência em São Paulo e no Rio Grande do Sul.
No vídeo mais recente, publicado na semana passada pelo @skate_anima, Lívia aparece apoiada em um equipamento adaptado, com o skate sob os pés. Giovanna, integrante da equipe de São Paulo, conduz a menina por trás, enquanto outros profissionais acompanham o percurso. Lívia teve uma reação emocionante e, no final, fez questão de cumprimentar e agradecer a todos.
Equipamento permite experimentar o skate
A estrutura usada pelo Skate Anima oferece sustentação ao participante enquanto o skate se movimenta. A atividade é acompanhada pela equipe, com equipamentos seguros e adaptados de acordo com as necessidades de cada pessoa.
O projeto surgiu em 2015, em Porto Alegre (RS), a partir de uma ideia do fisioterapeuta neurofuncional e skatista Stevan de Melo Pinto. Tudo começou depois que uma paciente com paralisia cerebral pediu para experimentar o skate em pé.
Stevan adaptou um equipamento usado durante as sessões de fisioterapia e colocou o skate sob a estrutura. A experiência deu origem ao Skate Anima, que passou a desenvolver novas formas de permitir que pessoas com deficiência também tivessem contato com o esporte.

Projeto reúne profissionais da saúde
A equipe é formada por profissionais de áreas como fisioterapia e psicologia. No Rio Grande do Sul, participam Stevan, idealizador da iniciativa, Júlia e Paula.
Em São Paulo, o projeto conta com Rodrigo, Giovanna e Ravelli. É Giovanna quem aparece conduzindo Lívia durante a descida registrada no vídeo mais recente.
O vídeo em que a menina com deficiência anda de skate adaptado mostra na prática a proposta do projeto: oferecer suporte para que cada participante possa experimentar o movimento e a sensação do esporte de acordo com as próprias necessidades.
Próxima atividade será no domingo
O Skate Anima segue realizando atividades aos domingos em São Paulo e região, sempre com acompanhamento da equipe e utilização dos equipamentos adaptados.
A próxima vivência está marcada para este domingo, 27 de setembro, no Sesc Guarulhos, na Grande São Paulo. A atividade será mais uma oportunidade para pessoas com deficiência experimentarem o skate com o suporte dos profissionais do projeto.

title: Deputy-minister’s ‘tip-off’ leads to labour raid on steel company
content:
A steel and tube manufacturing company in Ekurhuleni has come under scrutiny over its employment and financial practices, while a toilet paper manufacturer inspected by government officials on Tuesday was found to be compliant with labour and municipal regulations.
Deputy minister of employment and labour Jomo Sibiya said he had received a tip-off that the steel company, African Steel and Tube, had employed dozens of undocumented foreigners.
Sibiya said officials had been told that some foreigners who had been working at the factory the previous day were allegedly instructed not to come to work on the day of the inspection.
He also raised concerns about the company’s financial and employment practices, including an alleged R1.3m debt owed to the City of Ekurhuleni.
Sibiya said inspectors found that some employees were paid in cash over weekends, with those payments not reflected on their monthly payslips.
“Our inspectors found out that the company strictly pays its employees cash over the weekend. Meaning it is not added in their monthly payslip,” he said.
He was speaking during an inspection at the company alongside deputy minister of home affairs Njabulo Nzuza and Ekurhuleni mayor Nkosindiphile Xhakaza.
Sibiya said the inspection was part of efforts to strengthen enforcement of labour and immigration laws, as well as municipal bylaws.
Officials were also checking whether workers were at least paid the minimum wage, were registered with the Unemployment Insurance Fund and the Compensation Fund, and protected under the Basic Conditions of Employment Act.
Immigration officer Dipuo Maronetha, who inspected the workers’ identity documents, said 52 employees were present during the inspection.
“I can confirm that we arrived to find 52 employees. One is a Zimbabwean national who holds a Zimbabwean Exemption Permit (ZEP). There were no illegal immigrants,” she said.
Ekurhuleni mayor Nkosindiphile Xhakaza said the operation was important in protecting employment opportunities for local residents and ensuring businesses complied with municipal regulations.
He said the municipality was checking business and trading licences, building safety, zoning and land-use requirements, as well as whether companies were paying for services such as water and electricity.
“Law enforcement officers are working with immigration officials to strengthen compliance and ensure that businesses meet the requirements to operate in the city,” he said.
After the inspection at African Steel and Tube, the officials moved to toilet paper manufacturer Twinsaver.
The company was found to be compliant with the relevant requirements, including those relating to personal protective equipment, electricity and water.
“We are pleased to announce that this company is compliant. This is a rare find, which means it needs to be protected at all costs,” said Xhakaza.
“No wrongdoing was identified at Twinsaver during the inspection.”

title: Three Sisters Cross China to See What Keeps Their Family Apart
content:
Three Sisters Cross China to See What Keeps Their Family Apart
YUNNAN, Southwest China – Growing up in a remote mountain village in Yunnan province near China’s southwestern border with Vietnam, Zhou Lifang had only ever seen clouds from below. In late July, on her first flight, the 16-year-old saw them from above.
“I thought clouds were transparent because (my) textbook said clouds are made of water vapor,” she tells Sixth Tone. “But I didn’t expect them to be like a white wall. The clouds you see from the ground are in pieces, but from the sky they are one big mass.”
Lifang and her 14-year-old twin sisters, Zhou Lixin and Zhou Liyi, were among 145 students from Yunnan taking part in “Mountain-Sea Bond,” a four-day program in Shanghai that included reunions with parents working in the city.
The sisters are among China’s “left-behind children,” who remain in their home communities while their parents migrate for work, often placed in the care of grandparents or other relatives. China had 9 million such children in 2022, according to the 2023 Rural Education Development Report.
Born in Kunming, Yunnan’s provincial capital, the sisters have lived for more than a decade with their grandparents in a village in Malipo, a county in the Wenshan Zhuang and Miao Autonomous Prefecture roughly 400 kilometers away by road. Their parents, Zhou Yuneng and Zhang Shunfen, now work in Shanghai, where Zhou drives for a ride-hailing service and Zhang sorts groceries at a supermarket warehouse.
Smartphones have long allowed Zhou and Zhang to remain involved in their daughters’ lives from afar. They check in, offer advice, and try to mediate fights between the sisters. But they can see and hear only what the girls choose to share, and cannot always persuade them to talk.
Asked how well she knows her daughters now, the mother says they all like drawing, then pauses. “Close to zero,” she admits. “I don’t really know what they like anymore.”
After more than a decade of parenting largely by phone, Zhou and Zhang would spend two weeks sharing a 20-square-meter room in Shanghai with their daughters, their longest stretch together since the girls went to live with their grandparents.
On her own
Before the sisters left early that morning, their grandmother, Kuang Tianzhen, 64, tucked 50 yuan ($7) into each girl’s pocket, twice their usual weekly allowance. Rumors of scams in their border village had made her uneasy about the journey.
“Where will you stay in Wenshan?” she asks, the prefecture’s seat. “This is all reliable, right?”
After the neighbor’s car carrying them disappeared from view, their grandfather, Zhou Shucheng, 72, sat brooding outside the house for at least half an hour, staring down the rain-soaked road and gently petting the tabby cat his granddaughters had adopted.
Four hours later, the sisters arrived at a hotel in Wenshan for a predeparture meeting with participants from surrounding villages and counties. They would spend the night there, then continue to Kunming the next day for the flight to Shanghai.
“Are you Zhou Lifang’s parents? Have your three children arrived yet?” a trip organizer asks over the phone.
“I am Zhou Lifang,” she replies. “We’re already here in the lobby.”
Lifang was the only child in the tour’s WeChat group; everyone else was a parent. She had followed instructions about when and where to meet and confirmed the arrangements for all three sisters.
Inside the hotel’s meeting hall, grandparents sit beside children waiting to register while organizers address the crowd from the stage.
Elders are heard asking “Where should I sign?” and “Do I fill this part in?” At the line marked “guardian,” some pause, unsure whether to write their own names or those of the children’s parents in Shanghai.
One grandmother checks her granddaughter’s schoolbag, rebraids her hair, and films her on her phone. When organizers ask the adults to leave, she goes downstairs, then turns back and slips inside again.
Lifang sat quietly on one side of a wide pillar, her twin sisters on the other. Unlike many of the children around them, the sisters had arrived without a grandparent.
The sisters began attending boarding school around age 6. When home, they helped with farm work and tended the family’s wood-burning stove. Before they had smartphones of their own, they called their parents using their grandmother’s phone or a public telephone at school.
At 12, Lifang went alone to a hospital near her school for a tuberculosis screening while her mother guided her through the process over a video call.
“Sometimes I felt pretty helpless,” she says. “I would ask adults passing by for help and follow their directions.” On other visits, her mother advised her to follow a classmate who knew the hospital better.
When the village prepared to allocate plots of collectively owned farmland, Lifang took the call and passed the information to her grandmother. During school vacations, she tidied the twins’ room and called her mother when she needed money or help handling her sisters.
Her grandfather divides farm work and allowances equally among the three girls. But when they argue, he tells Lifang, “You’re the older sister. You’re the eldest. You should give way to them.”
The twins usually side with each other against Lifang, and a stray remark can set off a fierce argument. From Shanghai, Zhang tells her, “If someone hits you, whether it’s your sisters or your schoolmates, you should hit them back.”
Lifang sometimes goes into a room and locks the door instead. “Then they can’t come in,” she says. “They’ll play a game, and after that, everything will be fine.”
She has repeatedly asked her parents for a room of her own. When she wants to be alone, she sometimes sits on a swing her father built on the rooftop. On a nearby window, smiling faces the sisters traced with their fingers years ago remain visible beneath layers of dust.
“Sometimes I wish I could be the younger sister, not the older one,” Lifang says.
Close to zero
When the twins moved to the village at 3, they sometimes cried for their mother. Their grandmother would carry one of them outside and point toward Kunming, along the road winding over the mountain.
“I’d hold her for a while and tell her that her mother was there,” Kuang recalls. “Then she’d stop crying. They’re good girls, easy to coax.”
Their father had tried to leave the twins in the village a year earlier. He drove them there when they were 2, but couldn’t bear to leave them and took them back to Kunming.
By 2015, private kindergarten in Kunming cost 1,800 yuan ($250) per child per month, meaning fees for all three would have consumed 5,400 yuan of the couple’s roughly 6,000-yuan monthly income.
The family was also hundreds of thousands of yuan in debt after rebuilding the village house and paying hospital bills for the grandfather and one of the twins, who had spent several weeks in neonatal intensive care with meningitis. Because the girls lacked local household registration, or hukou, enrolling them in Kunming’s public schools was difficult.
For the next decade, their parents remained in Kunming, making the six-hour drive to the village every month or two for a weekend or holiday.
Years of installing wood floors damaged both of Zhou’s knees. The work required him to squat and sometimes kneel. “After every shift, I would get off my scooter and walk stiff-legged,” he says. In 2025, chronic arthritis forced him out of construction, and the couple moved to Shanghai, approximately 2,500 kilometers away.
When the sisters missed their parents, Lifang says, they video-called them. “Mom and Dad would always say they only had a few more days of work and would be back to see us soon.”
Over time, however, the girls stopped asking when their parents would return for good. “They used to say, ‘Mom, I miss you,’” Zhang says. “Since I moved to Shanghai, I hardly ever hear that anymore.”
In 2023, the couple installed a camera at the gate of the village house, primarily for safety. It lets them check on the grandfather and see when the girls return from school. They chose not to install one in the girls’ bedroom.
“I just feel that girls, after all, need some privacy,” Zhang says.
The mother also bought her daughters smartphones with large screens to make video calls easier and placed few restrictions on how they used them.
“Kids today are different from us back then,” she says. “Digital devices aren’t just for studying anymore. They have access to so many things on their phones. I don’t restrict them too much.”
The twins often decline their parents’ calls or hang up after a few sentences. Sometimes, one answers while playing on the computer, points the phone’s camera at the ceiling, and keeps playing.
Asked why, one of the twins says, “Just because I don’t have the patience.”
Every time this happens, Zhang just smiles and rarely lets her temper show.
“I feel that if I push too hard, I lose the right to speak,” she says. “I’m afraid they’ll think, ‘You didn’t raise me. You weren’t there when I was small, and now you want to tell me what to do.’ So sometimes I can’t be too direct. I have to be careful how I put it.”
When Lifang and the twins argue, the parents try to settle their disputes by phone, usually scolding both sides. Each girl comes away believing that she alone has been blamed.
“That’s because of the distance and what a phone call can’t do,” the mother says. “If it were face to face, a few sentences would clear it up.”
Unlike the twins, Lifang video calls Zhang almost every day and has her saved in her phone as “Dear Mom.” But she seldom calls Zhou. “Dad is quite busy driving day and night, so I rarely call him,” Lifang says. “I’m afraid of interrupting his work. I feel like I’m not close to him because he’s too strict.”
Even with Zhang, much of Lifang’s life remains outside their conversations. At school, some classmates seek her out for tarot readings, calling her “Master Zhou.” Others mock the way she speaks, comparing it to barking, and give her insulting nicknames.
Lifang spends nearly every break between classes drawing. She draws when she feels happy, angry, or embarrassed, and says it helps her relax. She keeps one sketchbook, which she rarely shows others, for times when she feels low.
One drawing shows a figure with its arms crossed and an X over its mouth. In the background, Lifang has written, “What if speaking is also a fault?”
“All I can do is draw them as ugly monsters,” Lifang says.
She closes the sketchbook.
“There are some words I cannot show,” she says. “Cannot.”
In another sketchbook, Lifang has created Yumeng, a cheerful girl from the sea who grows increasingly troubled as she tries to save a city from destruction. “Why should I, who am already living such a miserable life, have to save others?” the character asks.
Lifang also has a circle of friends her parents know little about. She met them through a nonviolent multiplayer game she describes as “healing.” Unlike the competitive games her sisters prefer, it lets players explore different settings, build homes and farms together, and talk.
“Besides my best friend at school, they are the most important friends in my life,” Lifang says.
Before boarding the flight to Shanghai, Lifang sent them an update: “I’m boarding now, so I can’t reply to your messages. I’ll send you some amazing pictures later.”
Under one roof
Two days after reuniting privately with their parents, all three sisters stepped onto a stage in matching pale green T-shirts and brand-new canvas shoes their mother had prepared before their arrival. “Mountain-Sea Bond” organizers had chosen the family for a letter reading at the Aug. 1 reunion ceremony.
Standing between the twins, Lifang began reading, with Zhang beside her daughters and Zhou watching from the audience.
“Before, I never understood why you were always away and could not be with us,” she reads. “Only on this trip, after coming to Shanghai where you live and work, did I truly understand how hard you work and how much you have given.”
When Lifang finishes, the audience applauds, and Zhou begins to sob. As the sisters come down from the stage, he pulls the twins close and continues crying until his face turns red. The twins’ eyes fill with tears.
“You don’t see your children often,” he says after regaining his composure. “And then suddenly you realize they have grown up all at once.”
After the ceremony, the family go to Jing’an Joy City, a Shanghai mall the sisters had long wanted to visit for its anime shops. Lifang taught herself to draw manga and now takes commissions through an app from clients across China, earning several dozen yuan per drawing. She hopes to attend one of China’s leading art academies, though she usually tells adults she wants to become a civil servant like her older cousin.
The program ended that day, but the sisters remained in Shanghai for the rest of their two-week stay. All five shared a one-room, 20-square-meter unit with a private bathroom and an induction cooker in one corner.
Zhou and Zhang had moved there at the beginning of the year, hoping the girls might eventually join them in Shanghai. Before the trip, Lifang had assumed the move had made her parents’ lives easier.
“Now that Mom and Dad work in Shanghai, the conditions are better, and the work is a little easier,” she says.
Zhou no longer installs floors, but his ride-hailing shifts often last at least 12 hours. “If you work less, you can’t make enough,” he says. “You drive for 11 or 12 hours, come back, charge the car, make something to eat, then sleep. The next day, you get up and repeat it. That’s the job.”
Zhang works similar hours sorting groceries at a supermarket warehouse and has no regular weekends. Sometimes they go an entire day without seeing each other awake; one leaves breakfast behind before the other gets up.
During the visit, Zhou took another week off from driving, while Zhang continued working. The parents would not allow the girls to go out alone in an unfamiliar city.
Before leaving Yunnan, Lifang says, “I want to help my mom sort groceries at the supermarket warehouse.” In Shanghai, she often accompanied Zhang to work, while the twins remained in the apartment.
One night, Zhang returned late from work and began tidying the room. One of the twins ran over and hugged her.
“Mom, I feel like you’ve worked so hard,” Zhang recalls her saying. The girl then began to cry.
“I feel like she’s really growing up,” Zhang says.
Despite all five sharing one room, the sisters argued less during the visit. Disputes that had been difficult to settle over the phone rarely became as heated in person, Zhang says.
Even before his daughters arrived, Zhou had been considering returning to Yunnan after another year in Shanghai.
“Whatever happens, I should go back and do whatever work I can, as long as we are by their side,” he says.
But Zhou has taken no steps toward moving and cannot say what work he might find near the village. Its karst terrain leaves little room to expand farmland, and 796 of its 2,172 residents work elsewhere, according to a village official.
Zhou and Zhang each earn about 8,000 yuan ($1,120) a month in Shanghai, though Zhou can make more by taking fewer days off. Returning would mean giving up the income that had drawn them farther from their daughters.
During their stay in Shanghai, the sisters called their grandmother about once a week. One day at a café, a blue parrot perched on Lifang’s shoulder. She has long wanted one like it, and blue is her favorite color. Lifang immediately called Kuang on video.
“Grandma, look what’s on my shoulder,” Lifang says. “Isn’t it impressive?”
“Behave yourself,” Kuang replies. “Where are the twins?”
“They went with Mom to work.”
“When will you come back?” Kuang asks. “How are you getting home?”
“Dad says he’ll drive us back next weekend,” Lifang says. “My school starts early.”

title: Tiny creatures moving 110 pounds of beach sand
content:
Sand hoppers, including species in the Megalorchestia group, are only about a few centimeters long. They commonly feed on kelp and other organic material washed onto beaches. During the day, they can remain hidden beneath seaweed or inside the sand. After dark, they emerge to feed and create burrows. “They have one of the highest rates of bioturbation of anything on the planet,” said UC Santa Barbara marine scientist David Hubbard. Bioturbation refers to the way living organisms disturb and move sediment.

Here's what researchers found
Researchers found that the activity of sand hoppers can result in an enormous amount of sand being shifted every day. The researchers studied sand hoppers at Isla Vista Beach, a stretch of coastline next to the UCSB campus. The animals do not simply burrow anywhere. They prefer a particular zone where the moisture in the sand is just right.Figure 1. Burrowing talitrids create a well-defined bioturbation zone on gently sloping sandy beaches in southern California. (a) Location of study site. (b) The burrowing zone (black dashed line) on Isla Vista Beach on a typical summer’s day. (c) Photograph of Megalorchestia spp. provided by Nicholas Schooler. (d) Rectangular metal frames used to estimate the mounding rate of burrowing talitrids. (e) Diagram showing the spatial arrangement of the 21 sampling plots (not to scale).
“They don’t like saturated sand that’s like liquid and their burrows collapse immediately,” Hubbard explained. “They don’t like the powdery dry sand above the high tide line. They like the Goldilocks sweet spot in between where the burrow will stay intact because the moisture in the sand is just right.” The scientists placed metal frames around sections of the beach after high tide and returned the following morning to see how much sand had been excavated.
What they found surprised them. The sand was almost buried overnight. The team expected to find evidence of burrowing, but the amount of sand moved was much greater than anticipated. “When we came back in the morning, we couldn’t even see some of the frames,” Hubbard recalled. “They were completely buried, and we were so glad we had put flags next to them just in case.”

After collecting and weighing the piles of excavated sand, researchers calculated that sand hoppers had moved as much as 50 kilograms of sand per meter of shoreline in a single day. “It was quite impressive and we weren’t really expecting that,” Baxter said. “I think for me that was the biggest shock.”
Sand hoppers could influence California beaches
The discovery is important because beaches are not static stretches of sand. They are constantly changing as waves, wind and currents move sediment along the coast. Sand hoppers appear to be another part of that system. Their burrowing can loosen sediment, potentially making it easier for wind and water to move the sand elsewhere.“It potentially increases the roughness of the surface of beaches, which has implications for the formation of landforms such as coastal sand dunes,” Baxter said. That could be significant because coastal dunes are increasingly being considered a natural defense against flooding and rising sea levels.
The sand hoppers' impact goes beyond physically moving sand. Their burrows can carry organic material deeper into the beach and introduce oxygen into the sediment.
“There’s a huge churn,” Hubbard explained. “If food like kelp or carrion gets deposited on the beach, it’s going to get buried by them, which makes it available to a different group of organisms.” The creatures also form an important part of the coastal food chain, eating kelp and becoming food for shorebirds and fish.
Researchers estimated what the sand hoppers' activity could mean across about 25 kilometers (15.5 miles) of Southern California coastline. The amount of sediment they potentially move is comparable to the daily sediment loads of some major Southern California rivers and to longshore processes that transport sand along beaches.
That puts an unexpected spotlight on animals that are usually overlooked when scientists study coastal erosion and sediment movement.
“I think part of that is the influence of animals on these processes is seen as quite temporary, quite localized and small,” Baxter said. “What we are trying to show in this study is that actually these activities and interactions are operating on a lot larger scale and that their impacts are really worth highlighting.”

title: Le Luxembourg renouvelle son soutien à l’aide humanitaire de l’ONU
content:
En marge de l’Assemblée générale des Nations unies, le Luxembourg a réaffirmé son soutien aux agences onusiennes engagées dans l’aide humanitaire.
Contrairement à des pays comme les États-Unis de Donald Trump, il n’est pas question pour le Luxembourg de réduire la voilure en termes d’aide humanitaire. Le Grand-Duc Guillaume l’a d’ailleurs souligné lors de son discours, devant l’assemblée générale des Nations unies. Rappelons que l’État luxembourgeois consacre chaque année 1 % de son revenu national brut (RNB) à l’aide publique au développement et à l’action humanitaire, soit 872 millions d’euros pour 2026.
Lundi, en marge de l’Assemblée générale de l’ONU, le ministre des Affaires étrangères, Xavier Bettel, également en charge de la Coopération et de l’Action humanitaire, a réaffirmé son soutien au système humanitaire des Nations unies. Trois nouveaux cadres de partenariats stratégiques pour la période 2027-2030 ont été signés avec le Bureau de la coordination des affaires humanitaires (OCHA), le Programme alimentaire mondial (PAM) et le Haut-Commissariat des Nations unies pour les réfugiés (HCR).
«Soutenir le multilatéralisme, c’est aussi soutenir les populations les plus vulnérables à travers le monde, ainsi que les agences de l’ONU qui œuvrent sur le terrain. Le Luxembourg reste un partenaire engagé des Nations unies et d’une action multilatérale efficace», a souligné le ministre Bettel sur les réseaux sociaux.
«Augmentation constante des besoins»
«Face à l’augmentation constante des besoins humanitaires, le Luxembourg poursuit son engagement en faveur d’une action humanitaire fondée sur les principes humanitaires et le respect du droit international humanitaire. La protection des travailleurs humanitaires, de plus en plus exposés aux violences et aux attaques, doit rester une priorité pour l’ensemble de la communauté internationale», complète le communiqué officiel du gouvernement.
Ces signatures ont eu lieu en présence de Tom Fletcher, le secrétaire général adjoint des Nations unies aux affaires humanitaires et coordonnateur des secours d’urgence. Le terrain pour le renouvellement du soutien du Luxembourg a été préparé fin mars lors de la visite du haut représentant de l’ONU au Grand-Duché.
Les deux autres signataires sont Carl Skau, le directeur exécutif par intérim du PAM, et Antón Leis García, le haut-commissaire adjoint chargé des opérations du HCR.
Les partenariats avec le PAM, le HCR et OCHA permettent au Grand-Duché de contribuer à la lutte contre la faim et à protéger les réfugiés et les personnes déplacées. Le Luxembourg soutient également une meilleure coordination de l’aide et le déploiement rapide de ressources là où les besoins sont les plus urgents.

title: Con la fumigación, Abelardo sembró una semilla de protesta en Putumayo y otras noticias
content:
Todo lo que necesita saber sobre el poder, la deforestación y la biodiversidad en la región amazónica está en la Silla Amazonía.
Estas fueron algunas de las noticias más relevantes de la región amazónica y el cambio climático esta semana:
- La Silla estuvo en Putumayo en medio del intento de la reanudación de la fumigación de cultivos de coca. Aunque se suspendió, esa decisión sembró una semilla de movilización social por los impactos sociales y ambientales.
- Arley Cañas, líder indígena del territorio Uitiboc-Asointam en Amazonas, en entrevista explica que no se oponen al desarrollo y el valor de los Territorios Indígenas para sostener la vida en todo el país en medio de la crisis climática.
- Gilberto Toro, director de Fedemunicipios, envió una carta al ministro del Interior, Rodrigo Lara, pidiendo revisar los actos administrativos que regulan y formalizan las Entidades Territoriales Indígenas para evitar que afecten la autonomía territorial de los municipios.
- El gobierno de Abelardo de la Espriella pidió revocar la suspensión provisional que hizo un juez del plan piloto de fumigación en Putumayo. Argumentó que es en zonas específicas, que el químico que quieren usar está autorizado y que hubo socialización.
- El presidente se reunió con autoridades tradicionales y líderes de pueblos indígenas en la sede alterna de la presidencia en Barranquilla. Afirmó que respetará la consulta previa, con ajustes, que quiere que las comunidades emprendan y se involucren en los proyectos desde el inicio y dejen de depender de subsidios. Oswaldo Muca, de la Opiac, participó y planteó fortalecer las ETI.
- El ministro de Justicia, Iván Cancino, presentó ante el Congreso las pautas del proyecto de ley de sometimiento de grupos armados ilegales. Aseguró que la primera muestra serán los 99 exmiembros de los Comandos de la Frontera que están en una Zona de Ubicación Temporal en Putumayo.
- Según el último informe de la ONG Global Witness, en Colombia fueron asesinadas al menos 39 personas defensoras del territorio y el ambiente en 2025, lo que ubica al país por cuarto año consecutivo como el más letal para líderes ambientales, con el 31% de las 124 víctimas en el mundo. Tres de ellos eran de Putumayo.
- El vicepresidente José Manuel Restrepo anunció que el gobierno priorizará la explotación de minerales estratégicos, como el cobre, el níquel y las tierras raras, uno de los cuatro ejes de la política minero-energética.
- Juliana Peña Niño, gerente para Colombia del Natural Resource Governance Institute, cuestiona en esta columna que la dirección de Ecopetrol esté tan ligada al gobierno de turno. Afirma que la empresa necesita autonomía técnica para tomar decisiones a largo plazo y se deben establecer reglas claras para evitar que quede envuelta en el ciclo político.

title: Joaquín “Kiki” Hernández, el fotógrafo que convirtió la magia de Jorge González en memoria de Cádiz
content:
Joaquín “Kiki” Hernández, el fotógrafo que convirtió la magia de Jorge González en memoria de Cádiz
Joaquín Hernández Conde, conocido como “Kiki”, siguió con su cámara a Jorge “Mágico” González desde que el salvadoreño desembarcó en España en 1982
La historia de Joaquín Hernández Conde “Kiki” con la fotografía comenzó en Cádiz en 1974. Apenas unos años después, en 1979, inició su etapa profesional como redactor gráfico de Diario de Cádiz, medio al que permaneció vinculado durante décadas.
Su cámara pasó por política, sociedad, cultura, Carnaval y numerosos acontecimientos que marcaron a la ciudad. El deporte también ocupó un espacio importante en su carrera y, especialmente, todo lo relacionado con el Cádiz CF.
Fue precisamente ese trabajo el que lo colocó frente a un joven futbolista salvadoreño que llegó a España después del Mundial de 1982. Se llamaba Jorge González, aunque Cádiz terminaría conociéndolo simplemente como “Mágico”.
Desde el primer día de Mágico en Cádiz
Kiki estuvo allí desde el comienzo. Según ha relatado el propio fotógrafo, acudió a recibir a González cuando llegó al aeropuerto de Jerez y posteriormente cubrió sus entrenamientos y partidos con el Cádiz.
Hernández no se limitaba a fotografiarlo los fines de semana. Su labor para Diario de Cádiz le permitía estar con frecuencia en los entrenamientos y viajar con el equipo, por lo que pudo documentar también una parte menos visible de la vida deportiva del salvadoreño.
Con el paso del tiempo, aquella relación profesional ganó cercanía. Kiki ha explicado que González incluso posaba para fotografías especiales y que entre ambos existía una relación frecuente más allá de las imágenes estrictamente necesarias para el periódico.
Su archivo conserva al salvadoreño en distintas facetas: regates, celebraciones, entrenamientos, ascensos, descensos y escenas alejadas de la competición. También consiguió fotografiar algunas de las acciones que terminaron formando parte del imaginario alrededor del “Mágico”.
Entre ellas está la denominada “culebrita macheteada”, una de las jugadas más recordadas de González. Hernández ha señalado que algunas de sus mejores fotografías del jugador no procedieron de partidos oficiales, sino de las sesiones de entrenamiento.
El vínculo tampoco desapareció cuando terminó la carrera de González en España. En 2018, Kiki condensó buena parte de ese archivo en “Mágico González retratado por Kiki”, un volumen de unas 200 páginas con más de 200 fotografías.
𝐅𝐨𝐭𝐨, 𝐧𝐨 𝐩𝐨𝐫 𝐟𝐚𝐯𝐨𝐫… 📸💛💙 ¿Quién se escondía detrás de esa mano? Mágico González, para muchos, el mejor jugador del mundo que vistió la camiseta del Cádiz CF. Hoy, a las 19:00 h, en el Centro Cultural San José de Puerto Real, proyectaré varias fotografías de Mágico dentro de «Historia Dorada del Cádiz CF». Una tarde para recordar al Mágico… y al Cádiz que nos hizo soñar. @CDC_CadizCF @CADIZ_CF1910
— Joaquín Hernández (@kikifotografo) September 11, 2026
La publicación recorrió las temporadas del salvadoreño con el Cádiz y sus posteriores regresos a la ciudad. Fue editada por el propio club gaditano con la colaboración de la Fundación Cajasol.
Una relación que sobrevivió al paso de los años
Cuatro décadas después de aquella llegada de 1982, fotógrafo y futbolista volvieron a encontrarse en Cádiz en 2022. La imagen de ambos juntos sobre el césped mostró que la relación había sobrevivido a la distancia y al paso del tiempo.
La historia tuvo otro capítulo en junio de 2024. Hernández viajó a El Salvador, acompañado por su esposa Carmen Romero, para participar en los actos de homenaje a González durante “Una Noche Mágica”.
Kiki volvió entonces a colocar su cámara frente al antiguo futbolista. Fotografió el recorrido de González por el museo dedicado a su trayectoria y los actos relacionados con el homenaje celebrado en San Salvador.
Durante esa visita recordó que había acompañado gráficamente al salvadoreño durante sus dos etapas en el Cádiz y describió a González como una persona cercana, sencilla y honesta. También sostuvo que nunca había visto a otro futbolista como él.
La cercanía ha sido expresada igualmente desde el otro lado. En 2025, cuando Kiki fue elegido pregonero de una tradicional velada gaditana, Mágico González apareció mediante un video para presentarlo, en el que mostró públicamente su afecto hacia el fotógrafo.
De esa forma, una relación nacida por una asignación periodística terminó convirtiéndose en un vínculo que ya supera los cuarenta años. Kiki siguió fotografiando a González mucho después de que terminara su última temporada con la camiseta amarilla.
Medio siglo detrás de la cámara y el reconocimiento en España
Reducir la trayectoria de Hernández únicamente a Mágico González, sin embargo, dejaría fuera buena parte de su obra. Desde mediados de los años setenta documentó las transformaciones de Cádiz con una cámara que pasó de los negativos analógicos a la fotografía digital.
En el ámbito deportivo reunió décadas de imágenes del Cádiz CF. Una de sus obras, “Historia Dorada del Cádiz CF”, reconstruyó gráficamente buena parte de la historia reciente del club mediante cientos de fotografías.
Su archivo personal ha crecido hasta superar el millón de imágenes digitalizadas y documentadas. En 2024 publicó “Memoria de un fotógrafo: 50 años de luces. Cádiz (1974-2024)”, una selección de casi 500 fotografías tomadas durante medio siglo.
La presentación reunió a representantes del periodismo, la fotografía y las instituciones gaditanas. Entre ellos estuvo Emilio Morenatti, fotógrafo español ganador en dos ocasiones del Premio Pulitzer, quien elogió públicamente el trabajo de Hernández y destacó el valor de su mirada.
La consideración hacia Kiki también se ha reflejado dentro del propio oficio. En 2015 recibió el Premio Paco Navarro de la Asociación de la Prensa de Cádiz, que reconoció su trayectoria profesional vinculada a la cobertura gráfica del Carnaval.
Un año después alcanzó otro hecho significativo: se convirtió en el primer fotógrafo que ingresó en la Real Academia Provincial de Bellas Artes de Cádiz. Hernández interpretó aquel nombramiento no solo como un reconocimiento personal, sino también como una valoración del trabajo desarrollado por los fotógrafos de prensa.
El deporte volvió a premiarlo en 2023. El Cádiz CF le concedió el Premio Juman de fotografía en la primera edición de sus premios periodísticos por “Marea amarilla”, una imagen captada antes de un encuentro entre Cádiz y Celta de Vigo.
Su ciudad dio un paso más en 2025 al concederle el título de Hijo Predilecto de Cádiz, una de las principales distinciones municipales. Ese mismo año recibió también el premio “Gato con Botas” por su labor de difusión del cadismo mediante la fotografía.
La prensa española ha terminado refiriéndose a Hernández como una especie de memoria gráfica de Cádiz. Sus fotografías han aparecido durante décadas en medios de comunicación y exposiciones, mientras instituciones periodísticas y culturales han reconocido el valor documental de su archivo.
Dentro de ese inmenso registro existe un apartado inseparable de El Salvador. Son miles de instantes de un futbolista que llegó a Cádiz en 1982 y que encontró frente a él a otro joven que comenzaba a abrirse camino en el fotoperiodismo.
Uno hacía magia con el balón. El otro llevaba una cámara. Más de cuatro décadas después, buena parte de lo que Cádiz recuerda visualmente de Jorge “Mágico” González continúa pasando por el objetivo de Joaquín “Kiki” Hernández.

title: Soulagement au Groenland et au Danemark après l’accord de sécurité signé avec Washington
content:
Jusqu’au bout, Danois et Groenlandais ont retenu leur souffle. Echaudés par les brusques revirements d’humeur de Donald Trump, les responsables politiques venus à New York – de Nuuk et de Copenhague –, dimanche 20 septembre, faisaient profil bas depuis que le président américain avait annoncé, deux jours plus tôt, qu’un accord avait été trouvé avec le royaume scandinave et son territoire autonome, clamant que son pays avait obtenu exactement ce qu’il souhaitait au Groenland.
Après des mois d’une crise diplomatique inédite avec Washington, provoquée par les menaces d’annexion de l’île arctique de 57 000 habitants par les Etats-Unis, le soulagement était donc énorme quand la cheffe du gouvernement danois, Mette Frederiksen, le premier ministre groenlandais, Jens-Frederik Nielsen et le président américain, Donald Trump, se sont enfin assis à la même table, mardi 22 septembre, au siège de l’Organisation des Nations unies (ONU), pour signer le texte de neuf pages, négocié depuis janvier.
Quelques instants avant la courte cérémonie, le président américain s’était félicité, devant l’Assemblée générale de l’ONU, d’avoir obtenu « un accord sans précédent », qui « confère aux Etats-Unis le droit de contrôler la sécurité et de répondre à tous [leurs] besoins sur ce territoire ». « Aucun adversaire des Etats-Unis ne sera plus jamais autorisé à établir une présence militaire au Groenland, ni à y réaliser des investissements sensibles sans notre accord explicite », ajoutait-il.

title: Mercado Ex Cuartel cumple 67 años, así celebrará con marimba, desfile y más
content:
Mercado Ex Cuartel cumple 67 años, así celebrará con marimba, desfile y más
El Mercado Ex Cuartel conmemora 67 años este viernes en San Salvador con una jornada que incluirá música, desfile y actividades para visitantes.
El Mercado Ex Cuartel celebra este viernes 18 de septiembre su 67 aniversario con una jornada abierta a comerciantes, familias y visitantes, que se desarrollará de 9:00 a.m. a 4:00 p.m. en el interior del recinto, según la Alcaldía de San Salvador Centro.
La programación anunciada incluye un desfile, música de marimba, pastel y otras actividades preparadas para conmemorar la trayectoria de este mercado ubicado en la capital.
La actividad se desarrollará durante siete horas y quienes deseen asistir podrán acercarse directamente al interior del mercado durante el horario anunciado por la municipalidad.
La celebración llega 67 años después de la inauguración del Mercado Ex Cuartel. De acuerdo con información histórica publicada por la Alcaldía de San Salvador, el recinto abrió sus puertas en septiembre de 1959.
Un mercado que funciona desde 1959
El Ex Cuartel se caracteriza por la venta de productos artesanales y tradicionales. La comuna ha señalado entre su oferta las artesanías, dulces, vestuario y calzado típico, productos que también han formado parte de las actividades organizadas por el mercado en aniversarios anteriores.
Un dato que permite dimensionar su actividad comercial es el número de puestos. En 2022, cuando se conmemoraron 63 años de su fundación, la Alcaldía de San Salvador informó que el mercado contaba con más de 500 puestos dedicados a comercializar productos artesanales.
Las actividades culturales tampoco son nuevas dentro de sus celebraciones. En aquel aniversario, la programación municipal incorporó música en vivo, marimba, batucada, una jornada médica preventiva y actividades infantiles.
Este viernes, la conmemoración continuará con una programación concentrada en un solo día. La invitación oficial destaca los encuentros, el trabajo y la tradición construidos durante las más de seis décadas de funcionamiento del recinto.
¿A qué hora será la celebración?
Quienes tengan previsto visitar el Mercado Ex Cuartel por su aniversario deben tener presentes tres datos: la celebración será este viernes 18 de septiembre de 2026, comenzará a las 9:00 a.m. y finalizará a las 4:00 p.m.
Las actividades se realizarán dentro del propio mercado. Entre lo anunciado para los asistentes se encuentran el desfile, la presentación de marimba y el tradicional pastel de aniversario.
La convocatoria es impulsada por la Alcaldía de San Salvador Centro y la administración municipal de mercados, que invitaron a comerciantes, familias y visitantes a participar en la celebración.

title: Côte d'Ivoire : près de 222 578 véhicules immatriculés depuis janvier 2026 grâce au numérique
content:
Côte d'Ivoire : près de 222 578 véhicules immatriculés depuis janvier 2026 grâce au numérique
Le directeur général des transports terrestres et de la circulation, Oumar Sacko, a annoncé l'immatriculation de près de 222 578 véhicules depuis janvier 2026, portée par la digitalisation.
Le directeur général des transports terrestres et de la circulation (DGTTC), Oumar Sacko, a affirmé qu’à ce jour, près de 222 578 véhicules ont été immatriculés depuis janvier 2026. Il a fait cette annonce lors de la tribune d’échanges « Tout savoir sur » (TSS) du Centre d’information et de communication gouvernementale (CICG), le mardi 22 septembre 2026 à Abidjan.
« Sur instruction de monsieur le ministre des Transports et des Affaires maritimes, le projet "BUS PRIMO" a été déployé depuis le 1ᵉʳ décembre 2025 afin de digitaliser toute la procédure d'immatriculation. Grâce à cette nouvelle plateforme, l’immatriculation des véhicules au Guichet unique automobile (GUA) connaît une progression remarquable. De janvier 2026 à ce jour, près de 222 578 véhicules ont été immatriculés », a déclaré Oumar Sacko.
Selon lui, l'ensemble de ces véhicules enregistrés se compose de 86 739 véhicules neufs, de 42 706 véhicules d'occasion et de 93 133 engins à deux et trois roues.
L’intervenant a assuré que ce nouveau système d’immatriculation vise à sécuriser les biens automobiles, à lutter contre la fraude et à interconnecter les bases de données.
D’autres mesures spécifiques ont été mises en œuvre pour répondre aux réalités du terrain. Outre les innovations introduites par la digitalisation, des facilités ont été accordées aux usagers. Ainsi, dans le cadre de l’immatriculation accélérée pour les véhicules neufs, plus de 21 619 véhicules ont été enregistrés à ce jour, avec 20 509 immatriculations générées et 13 582 plaques déjà posées.
Oumar Sacko a rappelé la mesure exceptionnelle d’immatriculation des véhicules privés des Forces de défense et de sécurité. Cette opération a déjà permis l'enregistrement de 18 706 véhicules, dont 10 856 effectivement immatriculés. Par ailleurs, afin de lutter contre la prolifération des motos circulant sans plaque, 40 253 motos ont été régularisées.
Enfin, le conférencier a annoncé qu’à partir du 1ᵉʳ octobre 2026, une opération d'envergure d'immatriculation des motocycles non encore enregistrés et d'installation des plaques pour les véhicules disposant de cartes grises sera déployée sur l'ensemble du territoire ivoirien.

title: La Peña Madridista de Ceuta responde a Mbappé, Vinícius y Konaté sobre las camisetas
content:
La Peña Madridista de Ceuta responde a Mbappé, Vinícius y Konaté: "No entendemos su actitud, solo se trataba de apoyar"
Basado en hechos observados y verificados directamente por nuestros periodistas o por fuentes informadas.

La Peña Madridista de Ceuta ha trasladado una protesta oficial al Real Madrid por la decisión de los tres futbolistas en el partido contra el Elche.
Mbappé, Vinícius y Konaté decidieron no mostrar el mensaje de apoyo a Ceuta en el inicio del partido ante el Elche, algo que sigue dando que hablar. Este jueves, la Peña Madridista de Ceuta ha trasladado una protesta oficial al Real Madrid por la decisión de tres de sus jugadores al no mostrar el mensaje de apoyo a los ceutíes en las camisetas que lucieron los futbolistas en el encuentro liguero.
"No entendemos la actitud de los tres jugadores, ya que aquí no era ningún tema político ni nada por el estilo, sólo se trataba de apoyar a una ciudad que lo está pasando mal", declaró a EFE el presidente de la Peña Madridista de Ceuta, Miguel Ángel Montano.
El dirigente ceutí comentó que han enviado el escrito al departamento de Peñas del club merengue.
"No comulgamos con lo que han hecho estos jugadores y hemos trasladado que el detalle no nos ha gustado porque hubiese sido mejor que no se pusieran la camiseta ninguno antes de hacer lo que hicieron", dijo.
Miguel Ángel Montano entiende que los futbolistas son "libres de hacer lo que quieran" y que no sabe "si será por algún tema de patrocinadores o algo pero lo cierto es que fue un gesto que no tenía sentido".
Recordó que España ha vivido otras situaciones parecidas como la DANA, el apagón eléctrico o los accidentes de trenes en Adamuz (Córdoba) "y ahora le toca a Ceuta vivir esta situación y este gesto de Vinicius, Mbappé y Konaté ha sentado mal", recalcó.
¿Qué opinas de que Mbappé, Vinícius y Konaté no mostraran el mensaje de apoyo a Ceuta?
Esta encuesta no es científica y sólo refleja la opinión de aquellos lectores que han elegido participar. Los resultados no representan necesariamente la opinión de los internautas en general o de los lectores al completo.
Los seguidores del equipo madridista en Ceuta vieron el partido en la sede de la Peña: "En un momento, y éramos unas 40 personas, pasamos de la euforia a la tristeza al ver lo que hicieron los tres futbolistas porque un poco de publicidad a Ceuta es mucho para nosotros en estos instantes", señaló.
El dirigente ceutí espera que el Real Madrid responda al escrito "porque es un club señorial y seguro que darán sus explicaciones".
La Peña Madridista de Ceuta, que se fundó en 1987 y que cuenta con unos 130 socios a pesar de llegar a ser más de 300 hace unos años, ha dejado claro que mantendrá su "fidelidad" hacia el Real Madrid.
Mbappé, el único de los tres futbolistas citados que hasta ahora ha hecho alguna declaración al respecto, justificó este miércoles su postura al decir que quiso tener un recuerdo para "todos los inmigrantes que han perdido la vida y también están en condiciones duras".
"Quería tener un pensamiento para toda la gente que sufre porque al final soy humano y no quiero poner prioridad al sufrimiento. Soy un chico que quiere lo mejor para el mundo que tenemos. Quiero dar un mensaje de positividad y de paz y espero que se solucione rápido", afirmó en declaraciones al diario As.

title: Quân y biên phòng kịp thời cấp cứu người phụ nữ hôn mê do bị ong vò vẽ đốt

title: These Black Los Angeles Residents May Soon Receive Environmental Reparations
content:
This story was originally published by Capital B and is reproduced here as part of the Climate Desk collaboration.
As a child in the 1950s and ’60s, Regina Martin became so used to the oil pumpjacks near her home that she assumed every child lived beside them. Everyone was made “sick to [their] tummy” by the sulfurous, rotten-egg smell that never seemed to leave, she thought.
Only until she was grown did she begin to see a possible connection between growing up on top of the nation’s largest urban oil drilling field and her own sickness and the asthma that affected her sister.
For over a century in Los Angeles and across the nation, Black people have been disproportionately likely to live near oil wells, the machinery that draws oil from deep underground. The pollution from these drilling sites are connected to birth complications, child development issues, respiratory illnesses, and cancer.
Now, a new California state law moves to turn that lived experience into a broader public-policy question: What does a state owe communities exposed to pollution for generations? And what happens when you can’t offer support to every family that has struggled through the harm?
California lawmakers have passed AB 1661, which would steer $5 million collected from penalized oil wells in Inglewood into direct cash aid for 1,000 nearby households with qualifying respiratory or reproductive health impacts. Some of LA’s Blackest suburbs and city neighborhoods, including Inglewood, Ladera Heights, and Baldwin Hills, surround the oil field.
The legislation, introduced by Assemblymember Isaac G. Bryan, is expected to be signed into law by Gov. Gavin Newsom by October. It sets aside enough money for payments of up to $5,000 for 1,000 impacted households under its initial structure. The money would come from the state’s community repair and reinvestment fund for people living nearest the oil field.
For Black communities living nearest to refineries, highways, landfills, and oil wells, this fund may signal something larger than one oil field or payment. It asks whether money can begin to repair harms accumulated across generations: lives cut short by illness, household wealth drained by medical bills and depressed property values, and the anxiety of raising children amid pollution.
Bryan and other supporters are calling it environmental reparations and say it is a model that could be replicated to make industrial companies help repair the damage borne by people living closest to polluting sites.
To Tianna Shaw-Wakeman, the environmental justice program director with Black Women for Wellness in LA, the law could provide a national organizing model. “My hope has always come at the community level, at the grassroots level,” she said. “I see how grassroots organizing has created long-term change in our local communities, and I see that that can be and is being replicated all over the country.”
For Bryan, who represents the communities surrounding the Inglewood Oil Field, the cash-assistance program is part of a longer fight over the field’s legacy. Bryan, the first Black legislator to chair the California Assembly’s Natural Resources Committee, said his constituents have faced lower life expectancies and higher rates of asthma and heart conditions for decades.
“The company has essentially just been extracting from the community with no investments in the community, no care in the community and what feels like no regard at times for the broader community,” Bryan told Capital B. “The community [is] due this repair, and it’s been long overdue.”
The measure builds on Bryan’s earlier legislation, AB 2716, which Newsom signed in 2024. That law requires the Inglewood Oil Field to close by 2030 and establish a penalty structure for low-producing wells. Low-producing wells can leak methane and other harmful gases into the air and water. To push operators to curb that pollution and clean up their sites, regulators imposed a penalty on companies that keep such wells operating. Bryan said operators are charged $10,000 per well each month, with the revenue directed into a community repair fund restricted to investments within 2.5 miles of the field.
The fund could eventually support affordable housing, urban greening, park infrastructure, and other community priorities, Bryan said. He described the cash program as a pilot that could help determine whether direct payments are the form of repair residents most want. “We know people are struggling,” he said. “We know one of the biggest tools against an increasingly unaffordable society is to just put more money in people’s pockets.”
As communities nationwide press for stronger environmental protections, California’s experiment could test whether government and industry are willing to move beyond preventing future harm and toward compensating people who have already lived with its costs.
“Community members who have been deeply impacted, whose health have been deeply impacted, have never gotten restitution for that in any sort of way. We deserve more than we have been getting,” Shaw-Wakeman said. “And as we transition our city, as we transition our county, part of that story has to be addressing past harms.”
At the same time, California has passed a law that would shield reparation payments from taxation. “California is actively preparing for the implementation of reparations programs,” said state Assemblymember Tina McKinnor, who introduced the legislation. “We must ensure that recipients receive the full benefit of these efforts.”
Three dozen community groups came together in support of the environmental reparations legislation. There were no groups in public opposition.
The legislation would not close the oil field or resolve the long-running fight over drilling in Los Angeles County.
Under the proposal, eligible households within 2.5 miles of the field could seek aid if a resident has experienced respiratory or reproductive health impacts. But the program’s practical reach will depend on how Los Angeles County designs the application process, what documentation it requires, and how it handles demand if more than 1,000 households apply. There are tens of thousands more households in proximity to the oil field.
Bryan said Los Angeles County was still working through how the assistance would be delivered. It could come as a lump-sum payment, monthly payments, or another structure, he said, and county officials were evaluating which approach would best serve families.
Shaw-Wakeman said Black Women for Wellness and its allies pushed for a process that does not force residents to clear burdensome or invasive hurdles to prove harm. The organization has urged officials to consider self-attestation rather than requiring applicants to produce medical records that may be difficult or costly to obtain.
That question of access may determine whether the fund actually proves relief or is another government program that excludes the people it was intended to help. Many families, particularly low-income ones, may be living with these illnesses without formal diagnoses.
The program also lands amid a larger debate over what should happen to urban oil sites once production ends. Environmental justice advocates have argued that closing wells is only the first step. They want operators held responsible for plugging wells, cleaning contaminated land, and ensuring that redevelopment does not displace the same neighbors who lived with the pollution.
As oil wells have closed in Los Angeles in recent years, rental prices and home values have risen, threatening to displace longtime Black residents.
“We can’t replace toxic oil extraction with gentrification,” Shaw-Wakeman said. “There is still a lot more to address beyond those 1,000 households. We’re trying to address the ways in which community members are still being harmed every day.”

title: Unsung Hero of Santiago de Cuba: From Groundskeeper to Avispa Mascot
content:
Alan Morales Pacheco holds a unique dual role at the Guillermón Moncada Stadium in Santiago de Cuba. He begins his day by meticulously preparing the baseball field and later dons the Avispa costume to energize the Santiago team’s fans.
This remarkable story was highlighted by sports commentator Pavel Otero on his Facebook page, where he referred to Morales as "an unsung hero with dual roles for the Santiago team."
According to Otero, Morales Pacheco has dedicated 25 years to maintaining the grounds of Guillermón Moncada and, for the past 13 years, has also brought the beloved Santiago de Cuba mascot to life.
Behind the Scenes at the Stadium
Morales is the first to arrive at the stadium, tasked with watering the field, painting the lines, compacting the pitcher's mound, and grooming the grass to ensure it’s game-ready. Once these duties are complete, he transitions seamlessly into his role as the Avispa mascot.
"He then dons the Avispa outfit to continue his double role," Otero noted, emphasizing Morales's dedication and hard work.
Not only does Morales work as a groundskeeper and mascot, but he also serves as a ball boy at the stadium. "He never stops working," Otero added in subsequent comments on his post.
Community Recognition and Support
The story has elicited numerous accolades from fans, who admire both the physical demands of Morales's roles and his long-standing commitment to Santiago baseball. "These are the true heroes without capes," one fan commented.
Another admirer praised his versatility, calling him "a true jack-of-all-trades." There have been calls for greater recognition of Morales's work: "His sacrifice deserves acknowledgment, better attention, and a good salary," someone suggested.
One supporter expressed, "Many blessings to him; he deserves recognition in a full stadium."
The Mascot's Memorable Moments
The Avispa of Santiago has been at the center of memorable events for fans. In June 2024, after Santiago de Cuba secured an 8-6 victory over Industriales, thanks to Harold Vásquez's ninth-inning home run, the Avispa’s antics caught attention. During the celebration, the mascot ran toward home plate and dove headfirst, causing the large red head of the costume to detach. The person inside, likely Morales given the timeline, quickly retrieved and reattached it.
Morales’s story is reminiscent of others who have long been the faces behind Cuba's beloved baseball mascots. In 2018, the tale of Osvaldo Reyes Pérez, known as "Chicho," came to light. He balanced his job as an operator at the Todo en Uno amusement park in Varadero with giving life to the Matanzas Crocodile.
Frequently Asked Questions about Santiago de Cuba's Unsung Hero
Who is Alan Morales Pacheco?
Alan Morales Pacheco is a dedicated employee at Guillermón Moncada Stadium in Santiago de Cuba, known for his dual role as a groundskeeper and the Avispa mascot.
What is the significance of the Avispa mascot?
The Avispa mascot plays a vital role in energizing and entertaining fans at Santiago de Cuba baseball games, adding excitement and spirit to the events.
How long has Morales been working at the stadium?
Morales has been working at Guillermón Moncada Stadium for 25 years, dedicating 13 of those years to animating the Avispa mascot.

title: Justiça libera R$ 2,68 bilhões para pagamentos atrasados do INSS; veja quem tem direito
content:
INSS: pagamentos correspondem a valores que deveriam ter sido pagos pelo governo, mas foram negados ou depositados abaixo do devido (Rafa Neddermeyer/Agência Brasil)
Repórter
Publicado em 21 de setembro de 2026 às 21h15.
RESUMO | O Conselho da Justiça Federal (CJF) liberou R$ 3,22 bilhões em RPVs para 278.063 pessoas que venceram ações contra o governo federal. Desse total, R$ 2,68 bilhões serão destinados a processos relacionados ao INSS e a benefícios assistenciais. Para receber, é necessário ter uma ação judicial ganha e uma RPV incluída no lote.
O Conselho da Justiça Federal (CJF) liberou R$ 3,22 bilhões em Requisições de Pequeno Valor (RPVs) para pessoas que venceram processos contra órgãos do governo federal. A maior parte dos recursos, R$ 2,68 bilhões, será destinada a ações envolvendo o INSS e benefícios assistenciais.
O lote inclui 278.063 pessoas, distribuídos em 218.651 processos. Estão incluídos casos de revisão de aposentadorias e pensões, além de ações relacionadas a auxílio por incapacidade e outros benefícios.
Os pagamentos correspondem a valores que deveriam ter sido pagos pelo governo, mas foram negados ou depositados abaixo do devido. Mas, atenção: o benefício ter sido negado pelo INSS, por si só, não garante o pagamento. É necessário ter vencido uma ação judicial e ter uma RPV incluída no lote liberado.
O dinheiro não é depositado diretamente na conta bancária habitual do beneficiário. Os Tribunais Regionais Federais (TRFs) recebem os recursos do CJF e fazem os depósitos em contas abertas individualmente no Banco do Brasil ou na Caixa Econômica Federal.
A data em que cada pagamento estará disponível depende do TRF responsável pelo processo.
A consulta pode ser feita nos sistemas da Justiça Federal, com o número do processo ou o CPF, conforme as regras de cada tribunal. Também é possível verificar se houve expedição da RPV ou liberação do pagamento.
Depois que o valor estiver disponível, o beneficiário poderá sacar o dinheiro na agência indicada ou, em determinadas situações, pedir a transferência para uma conta informada pelo advogado.

title: بعد ثلاث سنوات من الحرب… أطفال غزة يعودون إلى فصولهم الدراسية
content:
غزة- “القدس العربي”: عاد مئات الآلاف من أطفال غزة، السبت، إلى مقاعد الدراسة الحضورية للمرة الأولى منذ نحو ثلاث سنوات، في مشهد تختلط فيه فرحة العودة بآثار الحرب التي دمرت معظم المدارس وحولت بعضها إلى أنقاض، فيما يتلقى آخرون دروسهم في خيام ومبانٍ مؤقتة تفتقر إلى كثير من مقومات البيئة التعليمية.
وتقول منظمة الأمم المتحدة للطفولة (يونيسف) إن 98 بالمئة من مدارس غزة دُمرت أو تضررت خلال الحرب، فيما حُرم نحو 660 ألف طالب من التعليم الحضوري المنتظم.
ومع بدء العام الدراسي 2026-2027، أنشأت وزارة التعليم، بدعم من منظمات دولية ومحلية، عشرات المواقع التعليمية المؤقتة لاستيعاب الطلاب، بعضها في خيام أو مبانٍ معدنية وخشبية، فيما لا تزال مدارس أخرى تؤوي عائلات نازحة.
وبينما يحمل الأطفال أحلام العودة إلى الدراسة واستكمال تعليمهم، يواجهون واقعا قاسيا من نقص القرطاسية وارتفاع أسعارها، وغياب الكهرباء والمقاعد والتجهيزات الأساسية، فضلا عن الخوف الذي لا يزال يرافقهم بعد سنوات الحرب والنزوح.
ومع ذلك، يعود الطلاب إلى مدارسهم المؤقتة حاملين ما تبقى من أحلامهم، في محاولة لاستعادة جانب من حياتهم التي توقفت بفعل الحرب.

title: Vim fazer os meus sessenta e seis anos a Angola
content:
Uma terra em que o mais velho tem mais importância que o mais novo.
Aonde ser mais velho significa saber mais, ter mais experiência, ter mais respeito e ser ouvido.
Ao contrário da cultura ocidental em que se decidiu que a modernidade é mudar aquilo que os milénios de civilização concluíram ser melhor, em África, como na Ásia, os conceitos continuam a seguir aquilo que sempre foi reconhecido.
Não procuram matar Deus, não procuram mudar o género, não pretendem que quem fala mais alto é quem sabe e nem sequer pretendem que a juventude seja uma maior valia que a experiência.
Apenas pretendem continuar a levar a sua humanidade no caminho que foi passando desde que o Homem teve consciência da sua realidade.
É curioso como nós, na sociedade ocidental, continuamos a admirar a cultura e o saber dos povos que fazem a sua estratégia a longo prazo, que pensam o Mundo para a próxima geração e, ao mesmo tempo, pensamos na nossa vida apenas tendo em conta os prazeres que teremos hoje e promovendo as soluções do dia seguinte.
É uma esquizofrenia a forma de vida que criámos.
Nunca estamos satisfeitos com o que temos, mas, ao mesmo tempo, nunca estamos disponíveis para sofrer hoje para conseguir melhor amanhã.
Tratamos a juventude com mimo, convencidos que o prazer imediato é mais importante que a dureza da preparação dos jovens para uma vida com futuro, e acabamos por criar gente impreparada para enfrentar as dificuldades que sempre existirão na nossa vida.
E, para que a juventude seja bem tratada, determinou-se que os mais velhos devem deixar de ser a referência da experiência de uma vida para deixar aos novos a liberdade de fazerem aquilo que pretenderem.
A juventude é extraordinária.
É forte, é criativa, é disponível e é esperançosa e, por isso, deve ser projectada no trabalho para promover o desenvolvimento.
Mas a juventude só tem um sucesso consistente se aproveitar a experiência, a temperança, o bom senso o saber de quem já passou por essa juventude e que aprendeu mais sobre aquilo que é o Mundo.
Não devemos continuar a olhar a humanidade fazendo escolhas sobre quem é melhor e quem é pior.
Devemos sim, escolher juntar a criatividade e força da juventude com o saber e a experiência dos mais velhos.
Não devemos reformar os mais velhos, mas sim aproveitar o seu saber sem lhes exigir a sua força, aproveitar a sua prudência para temperar os riscos do desenvolvimento.
Devemos voltar a trazer Deus às nossas vidas, a razão às nossas decisões e o respeito aos nossos mais velhos.
Foi bom vir ser o Mais Velho a Angola!

title: CNIB AES à Agadez : Tarifs, pièces et enrôlement
content: © Gouvernorat d'Agadez AGADEZ,15 septembre 2026 — L'administration régionale d'Agadez accélère la modernisation de l'état civil. Le secrétaire général de la région, Souleymane Seidou Boulhassan, a inauguré ce mardi 15 septembre 2026 le dispositif d'enregistrement de la Carte nationale d'identité biométrique de l'Alliance des États du Sahel (CNIB AES), lors d'un rassemblement au siège de la Direction régionale de la police nationale. Un processus centralisé et hautement sécurisé L'introduction de ce document officiel garantit une protection accrue des données personnelles et renforce la sécurité identitaire. La procédure locale consiste à collecter l'empreinte et les paramètres biométriques de chaque citoyen à Agadez, puis à transmettre numériquement le dossier aux ateliers de fabrication centralisés à Niamey. Une fois imprimée dans la capitale, la carte physique effectue le trajet inverse pour être remise en main propre à son titulaire. Finalement, ce titre d'identité haute sécurité dispose d'une durée de validité de cinq ans. Modalités pratiques et pièces requises Par ailleurs, l'accès à ce service requiert la constitution d'un dossier administratif complet comprenant : Un acte de naissance ou un jugement supplétif ; Un certificat de nationalité nigérienne ; Un justificatif de domicile (certificat de résidence) ; Une attestation de profession et des photographies d'identité biométriques aux normes. Pour rationaliser l'accueil des usagers, la police nationale propose deux options tarifaires. L'instruction standard coûte 4 500 FCFA, tandis que la formule express s'élève à 9 000 FCFA. Les autorités ont intégré le paiement numérique via les plateformes financières mobiles Airtel Money, Amana et NITA pour fluidifier les transactions. Mobilisation civique recommandée Encadrée par les représentants civils et militaires de la préfecture, la journée d'inauguration a attiré une affluence nombreuse dès les premières heures. Face à cet engouement, Souleymane Seidou Boulhassan a encouragé l'ensemble des résidents du nord du pays à entreprendre promptement ces démarches, afin de généraliser ce titre d'identité souverain sur tout le territoire. L'inauguration de la CNIB AES à Agadez constitue une avancée technique notable, mais son succès dépendra désormais de la mise en œuvre concrète : régularité des opérations, maîtrise des délais et accessibilité pour les populations isolées. À défaut d'une logistique fiable et d'une information claire, le dispositif risque de rester une promesse administrative plutôt qu'un outil effectif de reconnaissance citoyenne ; les autorités locales sont donc attendues sur la rapidité du déploiement et la transparence des procédures. title: 特攻隊員2人のある悲話を基に 朗読ミュージカル「月光の夏」上演
content:
太平洋戦争末期、決別のピアノを弾いた後に出撃した特攻隊員の悲話を基に、戦争がもたらす不条理と命の尊さを訴える朗読ミュージカル「月光の夏」が、北九州市八幡西区の「長崎街道木屋瀬宿記念館 こやのせ座」で上演された。
日本の敗色が濃厚になっていた1945年5月、「死ぬ前にもう一度、思いっきりピアノが弾きたい」と願った2人の若者が佐賀県鳥栖市の国民学校を訪れ、ベートーベンのピアノソナタ「月光」を弾いた後、死地へ飛び立ったという実話に基づく。毛利恒之さんの原作で93年に映画化され話題を呼んだ。
ミュージカルは、北九州市在住のピアニストで作曲家の水上裕子さんが企画。ピアノ演奏と演出、音楽監督も務めた。2人の若者は東京音楽学校（現東京芸大）出身で音楽の道を歩もうとしていたが、志半ばでの学徒出陣だった。水上さんは「若者の夢が戦争によって突然断ち切られたことを思うと演奏家としてたまらなく切ないものがあった」と経緯を振り返る。
8月30日にあった公演には、市内を拠点に活動する朗読家や広島原爆の語り部の他、地元のダンス教室で学ぶ子どもたちも出演。会場を埋めた約300人が、水上さんが奏でる「月光」の調べと、朗読、舞踊が織りなす幽玄な舞台に見入った。
戦争を知らない世代にも当時の空気を感じてもらおうと、特攻隊員がピアノを弾いた当時の教室や、出撃拠点となった鹿児島県知覧町（現南九州市）にあった旧陸軍の基地へつながる線路とその向こうに広がる戦地の空などを背景に映すプロジェクションマッピングによる演出も取り入れた。
3人の子どもと訪れた八幡西区の会社員、村田雄一さん（42）は
「戦争の記憶をそれぞれの表現方法で伝えていくことは大切。朗読も歌もダンスも素晴らしく、子どもたちの心にも響いたと思う」と話した。【松本昌樹】

title: SENARE 2026 : une journée consacrée à la mémoire, au dialogue et à la paix
content:
SENARE 2026 : une journée consacrée à la mémoire, au dialogue et à la paix
La cinquième journée de la 5ᵉ édition de la Semaine nationale de la réconciliation (SENARE 2026), tenue samedi 19 septembre, a été consacrée à la transmission de la mémoire, à l’éducation citoyenne, au dialogue et au renforcement des valeurs de paix et de cohésion nationale.
La SENARE 2026 a consacré une journée à la mémoire, au dialogue et à la paix. Les participants aux Camps citoyens de la réconciliation ont visité le Musée des armées. Au Palais des Pionniers de Bamako, un panel a réuni responsables, acteurs socio-éducatifs et traditionnels sur les droits et devoirs du citoyen malien et la promotion de la paix. La clôture conjointe du Village et du Camp citoyen a rendu hommage aux jeunes des compétitions de drones, jeux vidéo et e-sport de l’initiative « Piloter la paix ». Des attestations ont été remises aux lauréats, aux participants de « Kalan Blon » et aux stands. Placée sous le thème « Éducation, culture et réconciliation : bâtir une citoyenneté résiliente pour une paix durable au sein de l’AES et de la sous-région », la SENARE 2026 a mis l’accent sur le rôle de la jeunesse dans le vivre-ensemble et la cohésion nationale.
